questions.stem: Given a = (3, −2) and b = (−1, 5), find a + b.
questions.explanation: Add corresponding components: (3 + (−1), −2 + 5) = (2, 3). Option (a) subtracts instead of adding the y-components.

questions.stem: In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. What is the vector AB in terms of a and b?
questions.explanation: To go from A to B: go from A back to O (which is −a), then from O to B (which is b). So AB = −a + b = b − a. A very common error is writing a − b instead.

questions.stem: Given p = (2, −3), q = (−1, 4) and r = (5, 1), find p + q − r.
questions.explanation: p + q − r = (2 + (−1) − 5, −3 + 4 − 1) = (−4, 0). Combine the x-components and y-components separately, being careful with negative signs.

questions.stem: Points A, B, C have position vectors a, b, c respectively. If AB = (4, 3) and BC = (−2, 5), find AC.
questions.explanation: By the triangle law: AC = AB + BC = (4 + (−2), 3 + 5) = (2, 8). Follow the path A → B → C to find the resultant vector A → C.

questions.stem: Given that a + 2b = (7, 1) and a = (3, −5), find b.
questions.explanation: Rearrange: 2b = (7, 1) − (3, −5) = (4, 6). Divide by 2: b = (2, 3). A common error is forgetting to subtract −5, getting (4, −4) instead of (4, 6).
